clue.text: Where there's little escape from current ebbing through broken bridge

indicators.note: the reversed current runs through the middle of the scrambled bridge, so one piece sits inside the other
something broken is in pieces, so the letters of bridge are rearranged
ebbing water flows back, so the abbreviation for current is read backwards

parts.note: AC is alternating current

explanation.surface: Someone fleeing across a collapsed bridge as the tide goes out finds no way out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' scrambles the bridge, 'ebbing' turns the current back, and 'through' sets it inside. The 'little' creature that cannot escape is a small bird, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A cage for a pet bird is a place where a small songbird has little chance of getting away.

clue.text: Refuse day without a drink

parts.note: bran is husk, the refuse left after milling grain

indicators.note: day without a means the letter A is removed from day

parts.note: taken as written before the deletion
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grumpy drinker refuses to go a whole day without a tipple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' drops the A from the day. 'Refuse' looks like a verb (decline) but is the noun: waste husks.
explanation.definitionFit: Brandy is a spirit distilled from wine, an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Send back a chap in debt

indicators.note: the chap sits inside the word for debt, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to be in the red is to be in debt
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A man who owes money is sent home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places the chap inside the debt word. Being 'in the red' means owing money at the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: A court that remands a prisoner sends them back into custody until a later hearing.

clue.text: Insect, bird and fish

parts.note: a cock is a male bird, especially a rooster
a roach is a freshwater fish of the carp family

explanation.surface: A naturalist lists three creatures: an insect, a bird and a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The list reads as three separate creatures; in fact the bird and fish join to make the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The cockroach is a common scuttling insect, a household pest.

clue.text: One that cometh about me with vessel stretching the rules to the limit

definitions.text: stretching the rules to the limit

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the man from the song goes round the word me

parts.note: 'The Gas Man Cometh' is a comic song by Flanders and Swann, so the one that cometh is the gasman
taken as written
a ship is a sea-going vessel

explanation.surface: A biblical-sounding figure arrives on a boat, bending every rule as far as it goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the gasman round 'me'. 'The Gas Man Cometh' is a well-known British comic song by Flanders and Swann about a series of workmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamesmanship is winning by dubious tactics that bend the rules without actually breaking them.

clue.text: Boris, a mad feature on the map

indicators.note: mad means crazy or deranged, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Boris, a madman, has become a landmark on the political map.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' rearranges BORISA into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An isobar is a line on a weather map joining points of equal atmospheric pressure.

clue.text: Steak cooked for Friday lunch?

indicators.note: cooked suggests the steak is prepared and transformed, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A steak is cooked for a meal at the end of the week.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges STEAK. Friday lunch is traditionally fish for Christians abstaining from meat, which steak is not.
explanation.definitionFit: Skate is a flat fish, the sort traditionally eaten on a Friday when meat was avoided.

clue.text: HM's place is for emollient speaking

parts.note: a balm is a soothing, softening ointment
oral means spoken, by speech

explanation.surface: The royal residence is said to be good for soothing talk.
explanation.walkthrough: HM is His or Her Majesty, the British monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Balmoral Castle in Scotland is a private residence of the British royal family.

clue.text: Phone back item from on board

parts.note: to ring someone is to phone them
the tail is the back end of something

explanation.surface: A caller rings back to ask about something left on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Phone back' looks like a single instruction (ring back) but splits into two pieces. On board means aboard ship.
explanation.definitionFit: On a sailing ship a ringtail is a small extra sail set behind the gaff of the spanker.

clue.text: Where life may cramp style?

indicators.note: style read as a verb means to fashion or design, so the letters of may cramp are shaped anew

explanation.surface: A place where the regimented life may cramp one's style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'style' rearranges MAYCRAMP into the answer, and the whole clue describes it: army life cramps your style.
explanation.definitionFit: A military base housing soldiers is a place of strict routine that restricts personal freedom.

clue.text: Porcelain maker keeps server in the family

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so the family word surrounds the server

parts.note: kin are one's family or relatives
AOL is a well-known internet service provider

explanation.surface: A potter's family business employs a waiter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps' puts the provider inside the family word. 'Server' looks like a waiter but is an internet service.
explanation.definitionFit: Kaolin is china clay, the main ingredient used in making porcelain.

clue.text: These people at it miss real issue

indicators.note: issue means outcome or product, so the letters emerge in a new order

explanation.surface: People who are busy at it miss the real point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' rearranges ATITMISSREAL into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Materialists are people devoted to possessions, who might be said to miss what truly matters.

clue.text: About one, tear over to a greasy spoon

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the reversed tear goes round the one
over means turned over, so the word for tear is read backwards

parts.note: to rend is to tear
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A man rips something up on the way to a cheap café.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns REND into DNER, and 'About' puts it round I: D-I-NER.
explanation.definitionFit: A greasy spoon is a cheap café, and a diner is a cheap roadside eatery.

clue.text: One carries the can, namely one creature after another

parts.note: sc. is the abbreviation of scilicet, Latin for namely
an ape is one creature
a goat is another creature

explanation.surface: The fall guy is blamed again and again, as each beast follows the last.
explanation.walkthrough: To carry the can is to take the blame. The original scapegoat in Leviticus bore the community's sins.
explanation.definitionFit: A scapegoat is someone who takes the blame for others, which is what carrying the can means.

clue.text: Medium of 18

parts.note: the comedy at 18-across, by Noel Coward, features an eccentric clairvoyant who summons the ghost of the hero's first wife

explanation.surface: The spiritualist in the play at 18.
explanation.definitionFit: The character is the comic psychic in Noel Coward's play who conducts the séance that calls up a ghost.

clue.text: Beef up leader for the church

parts.note: a rein is what leads and guides a horse
taken as written
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A leader calls for the church to be strengthened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beef up' is a verb meaning strengthen, not a meat.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinforce something is to strengthen it, which is what beef up means informally.

clue.text: Dead cursed vaguely without clarity

parts.note: ob. is short for obiit, Latin for died, used on gravestones

indicators.note: vaguely suggests loose and unformed, so the letters of cursed are scrambled

explanation.surface: A dead man cursed in a muddled way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vaguely' rearranges the curse word. 'Dead' gives the gravestone abbreviation, not a definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obscured is hidden or made unclear, lacking clarity.

clue.text: South American craft for hypocrites?

definitions.meaning: a dugout canoe of the kind used in South America and the Caribbean
read as two words, pious rogues: pi is slang for sanctimonious, so sanctimonious villains are hypocrites

explanation.walkthrough: PI is schoolboy slang for pious or sanctimonious; the question mark flags the split into PI ROGUES.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirogue is a long narrow dugout canoe used in the Americas.

clue.text: Polite British lack nothing in comedy play

indicators.note: a comedy turns things upside down, so these letters are put in a new arrangement

parts.note: O is nought, nothing

explanation.surface: Polite Britons who lack something feature in a comic play.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove O from POLITEBRITISH and rearrange the rest; 'lack nothing' says the O goes. The play is Noel Coward's ghost comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Blithe Spirit is a 1941 comedy play by Noel Coward about a séance.

clue.text: Grubby type featured by periodical?

indicators.note: by means next to, so the word for featured sits beside the periodical

parts.note: a mag is a magazine, a periodical
got here means got in, earned a feature

explanation.surface: A grubby sort of person gets written up in a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grubby type' is not a dirty person but the larva known as a grub. The question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A maggot is a fly larva, a grub, so a creature of the grub type.

clue.text: Copper advanced with unknown fulness

parts.note: a penny, abbreviated P, is a copper coin
money advanced is lent
Y is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: A policeman goes forward with an unexplained sense of abundance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman; it is the copper penny, P.
explanation.definitionFit: Plenty is abundance, a state of fulness.

clue.text: Flier annoyed with charges

parts.note: to be cross is to be annoyed
a bill sets out charges

explanation.surface: A traveller is angry about the fees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flier' looks like someone on a plane; it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The crossbill is a finch whose crossed beak tips help it extract seeds, a bird that flies.

clue.text: Power from above

parts.note: suggests divine power, but means energy that comes down from the sun overhead

explanation.surface: Divine power.
explanation.definitionFit: Solar energy is power derived from the sun, high in the sky above us.

clue.text: Chemin de fer not robust?

parts.note: FR is short for French, the language of the phrase
chemin de fer is French for railway, so rail

explanation.surface: Asks whether the French railway system is weak.
explanation.walkthrough: Chemin de fer is also a card game, but here it is literally French for railway: FR plus RAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone frail is weak and delicate, not robust.

clue.text: There's no time to agitate for currency

indicators.note: no time means the letter for time is left out

parts.note: to trouble someone is to agitate them

explanation.surface: A protester has no time to agitate about money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes T from TROUBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The rouble is the currency of Russia.

clue.text: There's nothing strange about a waiter

indicators.note: about means around in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: O is nought, nothing

explanation.surface: A waiter remarks that there is nothing odd about him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges O and STRANGE. The waiter is one of the two tramps who wait in Beckett's 'Waiting for Godot'.
explanation.definitionFit: Estragon is a character in Beckett's play who spends it waiting, so literally one who waits.

clue.text: Trees don't start to flourish here

definitions.text: Trees don't start to flourish here

indicators.note: the start of the word don't is its first letter
to flourish is to wave about with a flamboyant gesture, so the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: Trees fail to begin growing in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start' takes D from don't; 'to flourish' rearranges TREES plus D. The whole clue also describes the place.
explanation.definitionFit: A desert is an arid region where trees cannot grow.

clue.text: Station on GWR?

parts.note: GWR was the Great Western Railway; the stop is a Shropshire market town, and its name contains the word west from Western

explanation.surface: A stop on the old Great Western line.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shropshire town near the Welsh border had a station on the Great Western Railway network.
